title: One chikki for two, or four chikkis for seven: which share is more?
description: One chikki is divided between two children, and four chikkis among seven children. One half is written as four eighths, so both shares have four on top, and the board compares four sevenths with four eighths. Keeko doubts the answer by calling the bigger bottom number the bigger share.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the number of chikkis is the same, more children means a smaller share, so write one half with four on top and compare the bottom numbers. Watch for students who think a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction.

source: In which group will each child get more chikki: 1 chikki div
video_script.why: A learner compares one half with four sevenths by giving one half the same top number, four, and then comparing the bottom numbers.
video_script.substitution: the book's own groups: one chikki between two children and four chikkis among seven children
video_script.anchor: one chikki divided between two children, and four chikkis divided among seven children
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says four eighths is more because eight is a bigger number than seven, forgetting that eighths are smaller pieces than sevenths.
video_script.payoff_line: each child in the second group gets more chikki

final_answer.spoken: four sevenths is greater than four eighths, and four eighths is one half, so each child in the second group gets more

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, four eighths, four sevenths

names.{{NAME_4}}: the child who writes one half as four eighths

never_show: a tick on the first group
maths_rules: group 1: 1 chikki divided between 2 children, each child gets 1/2 chikki
group 2: 4 chikkis divided among 7 children, each child gets 4/7 chikki
4 chikkis among 7 children gives 4/7; the same 4 chikkis among 8 children gives 4/8; more children means a smaller share, so 4/7 > 4/8
4/8 = 1/2, so 4/7 > 1/2 and each child in group 2 gets more
slip: Keeko says 4/8 is more because 8 is bigger than 7; but an eighth is a smaller piece than a seventh
video_script.design: Two groups stay on the board. One half becomes four eighths so both shares have four on top. The same four chikkis are shared among seven children and then eight children.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; group 1: two children with one chikki; group 2: seven children with four chikkis of the same size; the words which group gets more? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.g1: two children and one chikki appear on the left
marks.g2: seven children and four chikkis of the same size appear on the right
marks.ask: the words which group gets more? appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it is again about sharing chikki.
<bookmark mark='g1'/>In one group, one chikki is divided between two children.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>In the other group, four chikkis are divided among seven children.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>In which group will each child get more chikki?

beats.on_screen: the two groups hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: group 1 shows 1/2 for each child; group 2 shows 4/7 for each child; 1/2 and 4/7 sit side by side; the top number 4 of 4/7 is circled

marks.plan: the top number 4 of 4/7 is circled and an arrow points to the top of 1/2

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>One chikki between two children gives each child one half.
<bookmark mark='sev'/>Four chikkis among seven children gives each child four sevenths.
<bookmark mark='plan'/>The top numbers differ, so we will first give one half the top number four.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 chikki between 2 children; 4 chikkis among 7 children
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one chikki is divided between two children, and four chikkis are divided among seven children.

beats.on_screen: To find: the group where each child gets more
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the group where each child gets more chikki.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: shares are 1/2 and 4/7; compare 1/2 and 4/7

marks.shares: the two shares 1/2 and 4/7 are written with a question mark between them

narration: <bookmark mark='shares'/>Step one, write each share as a fraction. The shares are one half and four sevenths, and we compare them.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 1/2 = (1 x 4)/(2 x 4) = 4/8; multiply top and bottom by the same number

marks.rule: the rule multiply top and bottom by the same number is written
marks.four: 1/2 changes to (1 x 4)/(2 x 4) and then to 4/8

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, give one half the top number four. {{NAME_4}} multiplies the top and the bottom by four, which keeps the amount the same.
<bookmark mark='four'/>One times four over two times four is four eighths.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 4 chikkis among 7 children gives 4/7; the same 4 chikkis among 8 children gives 4/8; more children, smaller share, so 4/7 > 4/8

marks.seven: four chikkis are shared among seven children, giving 4/7 each
marks.eight: the same four chikkis are shared among eight children, giving 4/8 each
marks.more: the words more children, smaller share are written between them

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step three, share four chikkis among seven children, and then the same four chikkis among eight children.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Each child gets four sevenths in the first case, and four eighths in the second.
<bookmark mark='more'/>With more children, each share is smaller, so four sevenths is greater than four eighths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4/8 = 1/2, so 4/7 > 1/2 and each child in group 2 gets more

marks.ans: 4/7 > 1/2 is written and glows, and group 2 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Four eighths is one half, so four sevenths is greater than one half. Each child in the second group gets more chikki.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two groups
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says 4/8 is more because 8 is bigger than 7; one seventh and one eighth of the same chikki are laid side by side and the eighth is shorter; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.pieces: one seventh and one eighth of the same chikki are laid side by side, and the eighth is shorter
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 4/8 < 4/7 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four eighths is more, because eight is a bigger number than seven.
<bookmark mark='pieces'/>But a bigger bottom number cuts the chikki into smaller pieces.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>An eighth is smaller than a seventh, so four eighths is less than four sevenths.
